lessons.title: What you saw, and what you heard

grammar.title: An impression from what you notice
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + そうだ/です; い-adjective minus final い + そう; な-adjective stem + そう. いい → よさそう. Use そうな + noun and そうに + action. Negative attachments need separate instruction; this lesson scores positive forms only.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve the earlier appearance pattern using visible or perceptible clues. It presents an impression or an impending event; it doesn’t certify a fact. Stem 降りそう differs from reported plain 降るそう. A preview can look interesting without you having seen the full film.
grammar.example: この短い映像は面白そうです。

examples.ja: この{短|みじか}い{映像|えいぞう}は{面白|おもしろ}そうです。
{空|そら}が{暗|くら}くなって、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}りそうです。
examples.en: The sky has darkened, and it looks as though it will rain.

examples.ja: {静|しず}かそうな{部屋|へや}で{練習|れんしゅう}します。
examples.en: I’ll practice in a room that looks quiet.

grammar.mistake: 面白そう is an impression; 面白いそう is a report. Do not remove the final い when reporting someone’s statement.

grammar.title: State what was reported, and by whom
grammar.formation: Hearsay: a plain verb/い-adjective proposition + そうだ; noun/な-adjective + だそうだ. Inferential/hearsay らしい follows plain clauses or noun/な-adjective stems directly. Characteristic noun + らしい is a different use.
grammar.explanation: Give the source when repeating a claim. そうだ reports information, while らしい can convey an inference or what you have heard. They overlap; there is no rigid certainty ranking and neither proves the report true. This unit contrasts the earlier N4 hearsay note with explicit source checking. Editorial sources disagree on the level of reported そうだ.
grammar.example: ハナの話では、映画は来週始まるそうです。
grammar.translation: According to Hana, the film starts next week.

examples.ja: ハナの{話|はなし}では、{映画|えいが}は{来週|らいしゅう}{始|はじ}まるそうです。
examples.en: According to Hana, the film starts next week.

examples.ja: {案内|あんない}では、{入場|にゅうじょう}は{無料|むりょう}だそうです。
examples.en: According to the notice, admission is free.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しい{店|みせ}は{評判|ひょうばん}がいいらしいです。
examples.en: Apparently the new shop has a good reputation.

grammar.mistake: A noun or な-adjective keeps だ before hearsay そう: 無料だそう. らしい attaches directly: 無料らしい. A form task may request one construction, but context doesn’t always exclude the other.

grammar.title: Explain an inference from clues
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective + ようだ/です; noun + のようだ; な-adjective + なようだ. Use ような + noun or ように + action when modifying. Purpose ように and changed ability ようになる are different constructions.
grammar.explanation: State what you notice and what you infer from it. A note on the door or a quiet room is a clue, not an absolute guarantee. ようだ is more formal than conversational みたい. Do not infer someone’s identity, feelings or a performance result with certainty from appearance alone.
grammar.example: 部屋が静かなので、作業は終わったようです。
grammar.translation: The room is quiet, so it appears the task has finished.

examples.ja: {部屋|へや}が{静|しず}かなので、{作業|さぎょう}は{終|お}わったようです。
examples.en: The room is quiet, so it appears the task has finished.

examples.ja: ここは{練習|れんしゅう}のための{教室|きょうしつ}のようです。
examples.en: This appears to be a classroom used for practice.

examples.ja: {表情|ひょうじょう}から、{緊張|きんちょう}しているようです。
examples.en: From the facial expression, the person appears to be nervous.

grammar.mistake: Nouns need の and な-adjectives need な before よう. An inference is not confirmation; check the record if the distinction matters.

grammar.title: A conversational likeness or inference
grammar.formation: Plain clauses or noun/な-adjective stems + みたいだ/です; みたいな + noun; みたいに + action. This grammatical みたい is not 見たい meaning “want to see”.
grammar.explanation: Friends often use みたい for a likeness or inference. ようだ can describe the same situation more formally, so don’t assume that one must always be wrong. Compare the noun attachments: 教室みたい and 教室のよう. A costume can resemble a profession without making its wearer a member of it.
grammar.example: この衣装は先生の服みたいです。
grammar.translation: This costume looks like a teacher’s clothes.

examples.ja: この{衣装|いしょう}は{先生|せんせい}の{服|ふく}みたいです。
examples.en: This costume looks like a teacher’s clothes.

examples.ja: {教室|きょうしつ}みたいな{部屋|へや}で{撮影|さつえい}します。
examples.en: We’ll film in a room resembling a classroom.

examples.ja: {通話|つうわ}が{切|き}れたみたいです。
examples.en: It seems the call has dropped.

grammar.mistake: Do not add の before みたい after a noun. 教室みたいな部屋 is a likeness, not proof that the room is officially a classroom.

grammar.title: A perceived trait, not an identity
grammar.formation: Selected established noun/stem + っぽい forms become い-adjectives: っぽく, っぽかった, っぽくない. Examples here: 黒っぽい、忘れっぽい、大人っぽい. This suffix is not freely attachable to every verb or adjective.
grammar.explanation: Describe a perceived colour, manner or tendency with care. 黒っぽい can be nearly black without being exactly black. 忘れっぽい describes a tendency, not a diagnosis. Compare a resemblance with the typical/characteristic noun + らしい use; neither justifies a stereotype about a group.
grammar.example: 黒っぽい衣装を選びました。
grammar.translation: I chose a dark, almost-black costume.

examples.ja: {黒|くろ}っぽい{衣装|いしょう}を{選|えら}びました。
examples.en: I chose a dark, almost-black costume.

examples.ja: {忘|わす}れっぽいので、{台詞|せりふ}のメモを{使|つか}います。
examples.en: I tend to forget, so I use notes for my lines.

examples.ja: この{登場人物|とうじょうじんぶつ}は{大人|おとな}っぽい{話|はな}し{方|かた}をします。
examples.en: This character speaks in a mature-sounding way.

grammar.mistake: Conjugate the new adjective: 黒っぽくない, not 黒っぽいじゃない. Learn established combinations instead of inventing new ones from any verb.

dialogues.title: Misaki checks the film rumour
dialogues.scene: Kenta introduces his friend Misaki to Bao. They discuss a student film preview and separate an impression from a report. The screening date is not independently verified in this scene.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: バオ、こちらは{友達|ともだち}の{美咲|みさき}だよ。{映画|えいが}が{好|す}きなんだ。
lines.romaji: Bao, kochira wa tomodachi no Misaki da yo. Eiga ga suki nan da.
lines.meaning: Bao, this is my friend Misaki. She likes films.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {美咲|みさき}です。よろしくね。あの{録画|ろくが}した{映像|えいぞう}、{面白|おもしろ}そうだね。
lines.romaji: Misaki desu. Yoroshiku ne. Ano rokuga shita eizō, omoshirosō da ne.
lines.meaning: I’m Misaki. Nice to meet you. That recorded video looks interesting.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {短|みじか}い{紹介|しょうかい}だけ{見|み}たよ。{映画|えいが}{全部|ぜんぶ}は、まだ{見|み}ていない。
lines.romaji: Mijikai shōkai dake mita yo. Eiga zenbu wa, mada mite inai.
lines.meaning: I saw only the short introduction. I haven’t seen the whole film yet.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: ハナの{話|はなし}では、{来週|らいしゅう}{始|はじ}まるそうだよ。
lines.romaji: Hana no hanashi de wa, raishū hajimaru sō da yo.
lines.meaning: According to Hana, it starts next week.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: その{情報|じょうほう}は、{確認|かくにん}した？
lines.romaji: Sono jōhō wa, kakunin shita?
lines.meaning: Have you checked that information?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: まだだよ。{評判|ひょうばん}はいいらしいけど、{日|ひ}にちは{確|たし}かめたい。
lines.romaji: Mada da yo. Hyōban wa ii rashii kedo, hinichi wa tashikametai.
lines.meaning: Not yet. Apparently its reputation is good, but I want to check the date.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {通話|つうわ}が{終|お}わったら、ハナに{案内|あんない}を{送|おく}ってもらおう。
lines.romaji: Tsūwa ga owattara, Hana ni annai o okutte moraō.
lines.meaning: When the call finishes, let’s ask Hana to send the notice.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。{案内|あんない}を{保存|ほぞん}しとくよ。{日|ひ}にちが{決|き}まったら{教|おし}えて。
lines.romaji: Un. Annai o hozon shitoku yo. Hinichi ga kimattara oshiete.
lines.meaning: I’ll save the notice. Let me know when the date’s settled.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {評判|ひょうばん}がいいから、{早|はや}く{見|み}たいね。{噂|うわさ}では{続編|ぞくへん}もあるらしいよ。
lines.romaji: Hyōban ga ii kara, hayaku mitai ne. Uwasa de wa zokuhen mo aru rashii yo.
lines.meaning: It’s getting good reviews, so I can’t wait to see it. I hear there might be a sequel too.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: じゃ、ハナの{返事|へんじ}を{待|ま}とう。{来週|らいしゅう}なら{土曜日|どようび}が{空|あ}いてるよ。
lines.romaji: Ja, Hana no henji o matō. Raishū nara doyōbi ga aiteru yo.
lines.meaning: Let’s wait for Hana’s reply. I’m free next Saturday.

dialogues.title: Costume, role, and the person wearing it
dialogues.scene: Later, Misaki shares a student film rehearsal. Clothing, a fictional role and a performer’s self-described tendency are separate things.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: これが{撮影|さつえい}で{使|つか}う{衣装|いしょう}だよ。{先生|せんせい}の{服|ふく}みたいでしょう。
lines.romaji: Kore ga satsuei de tsukau ishō da yo. Sensei no fuku mitai deshō.
lines.meaning: This is the costume for filming. It looks like a teacher’s clothes, does it not?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん、{黒|くろ}っぽいね。{先生|せんせい}の{役|やく}なの？
lines.romaji: Un, kuroppoi ne. Sensei no yaku na no?
lines.meaning: Yes, it’s dark, almost black. Is it a teacher’s role?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: そうだよ。{先生|せんせい}の{役|やく}は{初|はじ}めてだから、ちょっと{緊張|きんちょう}してる。
lines.romaji: Sō da yo. Sensei no yaku wa hajimete da kara, chotto kinchō shiteru.
lines.meaning: Yes. It’s my first time playing a teacher, so I’m a little nervous.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {衣装|いしょう}、{似合|にあ}ってるね。{台詞|せりふ}はもう{覚|おぼ}えた？
lines.romaji: Ishō, niatteru ne. Serifu wa mō oboeta?
lines.meaning: The costume suits you. Have you learnt your lines yet?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: うん。{台詞|せりふ}は{短|みじか}いけど、{私|わたし}は{忘|わす}れっぽいから、メモを{使|つか}う。
lines.romaji: Un. Serifu wa mijikai kedo, watashi wa wasureppoi kara, memo o tsukau.
lines.meaning: Yes. The lines are short, but I tend to forget, so I use notes.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {台詞|せりふ}を{区切|くぎ}って{繰|く}り{返|かえ}すといいよ。
lines.romaji: Serifu o kugitte kurikaesu to ii yo.
lines.meaning: It helps to divide the lines into sections and repeat them.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: その{工夫|くふう}、{試|ため}してみる。{練習|れんしゅう}も{録画|ろくが}しよう。
lines.romaji: Sono kufū, tameshite miru. Renshū mo rokuga shiyō.
lines.meaning: I’ll try that idea. Let’s record the practice too.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: あとで{保存|ほぞん}して、{話|はな}し{方|かた}を{見直|みなお}せるね。
lines.romaji: Ato de hozon shite, hanashikata o minaoseru ne.
lines.meaning: We can save it afterward and review how you speak.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {休憩|きゅうけい}も{取|と}ろう。お{茶|ちゃ}が{冷|さ}めないうちに{飲|の}みたい。
lines.romaji: Kyūkei mo torō. Ocha ga samenai uchi ni nomitai.
lines.meaning: Let’s take a break too. I want to drink the tea before it cools.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: いいね。{休憩|きゅうけい}の{後|あと}で、{最初|さいしょ}の{場面|ばめん}から{撮|と}ってみよう。
lines.romaji: Ii ne. Kyūkei no ato de, saisho no bamen kara totte miyō.
lines.meaning: Good idea. After the break, let’s try filming from the first scene.

readings.title: A message separating impressions and facts
paragraphs: レンへ。{今日|きょう}、ケンタの{友達|ともだち}の{美咲|みさき}と{話|はな}した。{映画|えいが}の{短|みじか}い{紹介|しょうかい}を{見|み}て、{面白|おもしろ}そうだと{思|おも}った。でも、{全部|ぜんぶ}はまだ{見|み}ていない。ハナの{話|はなし}では{来週|らいしゅう}{始|はじ}まるそうだが、{日|ひ}にちはまだ{確認|かくにん}していない。{案内|あんない}をもらってから{予定|よてい}を{決|き}める。

{美咲|みさき}は{学生|がくせい}の{映画|えいが}で{先生|せんせい}の{役|やく}をする。{衣装|いしょう}は{黒|くろ}っぽく、{先生|せんせい}の{服|ふく}みたいだ。でも、{本物|ほんもの}の{先生|せんせい}ではない。{忘|わす}れっぽいので、{台詞|せりふ}のメモを{使|つか}うと{言|い}っていた。{短|みじか}く{区切|くぎ}って{繰|く}り{返|かえ}す{練習|れんしゅう}を{勧|すす}めた。{録画|ろくが}を{保存|ほぞん}して、あとで{話|はな}し{方|かた}を{見直|みなお}す。{見|み}た{目|め}の{印象|いんしょう}と{事実|じじつ}は{分|わ}けて{考|かんが}えたい。

glosses.meaning: doing; part of a compound action

exercises.prompt: How much of the film has Bao seen?
exercises.explain: Bao explicitly says only the short introduction, not the whole film.

exercises.prompt: Who is named as the source for next week’s start?
exercises.explain: Misaki says ハナの話では before the reported information.

exercises.prompt: Has Misaki independently checked the date?
options: Not yet; she wants to check it
Yes; she already holds a ticket
The scene says the screening ended
exercises.explain: まだだよ and 日にちは確かめたい state the remaining check.

exercises.context: Form practice: give an impression from a preview with appearance そう. Use 面白い, not the reported-statement construction.
exercises.line: この{紹介|しょうかい}は＿＿そうです。
exercises.explain: Appearance そう follows the adjective stem. The full adjective would give a report.

exercises.context: Form practice: relay a notice that says admission is free using hearsay そう. Choose the noun predicate form.
exercises.line: {案内|あんない}では、{入場|にゅうじょう}は＿＿そうです。
exercises.explain: The hearsay proposition keeps the copula だ after 無料.

exercises.context: Form practice: use ようだ to say the room appears to be a classroom. Select the nominal connector.
exercises.line: ここは{教室|きょうしつ}＿＿ようです。
exercises.explain: A noun uses のよう; a な-adjective would use なよう.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki: you have not checked the information yet and will check the notice before deciding.
exercises.line: その{情報|じょうほう}、もう{確認|かくにん}した？
options: まだだよ。{案内|あんない}を{確認|かくにん}してから{決|き}める。
うん、もう{全部|ぜんぶ}{確認|かくにん}した。
うん、{映画|えいが}は{昨日|きのう}{終|お}わった。
exercises.explain: Only the first reply preserves the explicitly unconfirmed state.

exercises.meaning: According to Hana, the film starts next week.
tiles: {来週|らいしゅう}{始|はじ}まる
exercises.explain: The reported plain clause 始まる precedes そう; the source is named first.

options: Bao’s actual teacher at the university
exercises.explain: Misaki says 先生の役は初めて: it’s her first time portraying a teacher.

options: She says she tends to forget the lines
She has already memorised every line
exercises.explain: She says 忘れっぽいからメモを使う; this is a self-described tendency.

exercises.prompt: What practice method does Bao suggest?
options: Divide the lines into sections and repeat them
Throw away the notes before rehearsal
exercises.explain: Bao suggests 区切って繰り返す.

exercises.context: Form practice: say the room resembles a classroom using みたいな + noun. Select what follows the noun 教室 directly.
exercises.line: {教室|きょうしつ}＿＿{部屋|へや}で{撮影|さつえい}します。
exercises.explain: みたい attaches directly to the noun, then な modifies 部屋.

exercises.context: Form practice: negate the established adjective 黒っぽい. The costume is not dark or almost black.
exercises.line: この{衣装|いしょう}は＿＿です。
exercises.explain: The い-adjective negative is っぽくない; these distractors test form explicitly.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki: acknowledge the teacher as a fictional role, without claiming she is a real teacher.
exercises.line: {先生|せんせい}の{役|やく}だよ。{本物|ほんもの}の{先生|せんせい}じゃない。
options: うん、{映画|えいが}の{役|やく}なんだね。
うん、{本物|ほんもの}の{先生|せんせい}なんだね。
うん、{映画|えいが}には{出|で}ないんだね。
exercises.explain: The first reply preserves the role/reality distinction; the others contradict it.

exercises.meaning: I chose a dark, almost-black costume for filming.
exercises.explain: The characteristic adjective modifies 衣装; the purpose clause recycles unit 1.

exercises.prompt: Which statement preserves the message’s status of the screening date?
options: Next week is reported, but the calendar date is not yet checked
exercises.explain: ハナの話では…そうだ is a report, followed by 日にちはまだ確認していない.
exercises.context: Use the message, not an assumption about a rumour.

exercises.prompt: What does the message say about Misaki?
options: She will portray a teacher in a student film
She has become Bao’s actual teacher
She will attend an exam as a teacher
exercises.explain: 先生の役をする is explicitly separated from 本物の先生ではない.

exercises.prompt: Which pair of actions is recommended and then planned?
options: Repeat short sections; save and review the recording
Confirm an exam score; buy a costume
exercises.explain: The writer recommends short repeated sections, then plans saving and reviewing the recording.
exercises.context: Read the second paragraph; separate the two actions.

grammar: inference ようだ / らしい
みたい / selected っぽい
watch.prompt: Optionally save a line reporting someone else’s information and a line describing an impression from your own clip. Note the stated source or clue. This observes language, not the truth of the fictional claim or your proficiency.
